items.prompt: An order holds 2 units at 10.00 with a 5.00 discount. The user saves, exits and restarts the delivered app. What does menu 8 show?
items.answer: Subtotal 20.00, discount 5.00, total 15.00, all as they were before
distractors: Subtotal 20.00, discount 0.00, total 20.00, as reload clamps the discount
Subtotal 20.00, discount 5.00, total 20.00, as totals are cached on save
Nothing: startup stops, as a saved discount fails the empty-order check
items.explanation: parseRows groups all item rows by order and calls Order.restore with the complete list, so the discount is checked against the full 20.00 subtotal. The regression test reloads 5.00 and 15.00. (The original app reset it to 0.)

items.prompt: An order has 3 units at 10.00 and a discount of 25.00. Menu 14 asks to change the quantity to 2. What happens?
items.answer: Refused, so quantity stays 3, discount 25.00 and total 5.00
distractors: Accepted, with the discount lowered to 20.00 and a total of 0.00
Accepted, with quantity 2 and a total of -5.00 until the next save
Accepted, with the discount cleared and a total of 20.00
items.explanation: setItemQuantity builds a candidate line and checks the proposed subtotal (20.00) against the discount before replacing anything; validateSubtotal throws "Reduce the discount before reducing the subtotal." Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: An order has moved to PAID. The user applies a new 1.00 discount with menu 10. What does the app print?
items.answer: Could not apply discount: Orders in PAID status cannot be edited.
distractors: Discount applied.
Could not apply discount: Discount cannot exceed subtotal.
Could not apply discount: Invalid order status transition from PAID.
items.explanation: applyDiscount calls ensureEditable, and isEditable is true only for DRAFT and SUBMITTED. Verified in a probe; the regression test checks the same rule for adding items.

items.prompt: A caller reads an order with service.findById, then calls getItems().get(0).setQuantity(99) on the result. What changes?
items.answer: Nothing stored, as the order and its items were both handed out as copies
distractors: The stored order, whose total grows because the item object is shared
The stored line quantity only, while the cached total stays the same
Nothing, because setQuantity throws on an item that was read from a list
items.explanation: findById returns order.copy(), and getItems maps every line through OrderItem.copy. setQuantity succeeds on that copy only. Verified in a probe (stored total still 15.00).

items.prompt: A brand-new DRAFT order has no items. In menu 11 the user chooses SUBMITTED. What does the app print?
items.answer: Could not update order status: An empty order cannot enter that status.
distractors: Order status updated.
Could not update order status: An empty order cannot be moved to SUBMITTED.
Could not update order status: Invalid status transition from DRAFT to SUBMITTED.
items.explanation: The service check for empty orders names only PAID and SHIPPED, so it passes; Order.setStatus then applies requiresItems, which includes SUBMITTED, and throws its own message. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: A SUBMITTED order has exactly one line and no discount. The user removes that line with menu 7. What happens?
items.answer: Refused, since a submitted order must keep at least one item
distractors: The line is removed and the order goes back to the DRAFT status
The line is removed, leaving an empty SUBMITTED order
Refused, since SUBMITTED orders cannot be edited at all
items.explanation: removeItemByProductId checks status == SUBMITTED && items.size() == 1 and throws "A submitted order must keep at least one item." SUBMITTED is still editable for other changes; a DRAFT order may lose its last line.

items.prompt: An order has 3 units of a 10.00 notebook. The user adds the same notebook again with quantity 1. What does the order hold?
items.answer: One notebook line of 4 units, still at its own 10.00 price snapshot
distractors: Two notebook lines, 3 units and 1 unit, each with its own price snapshot
One notebook line of 1 unit, as adding a product again replaces its line
Nothing new, as a product that is already on the order is refused
items.explanation: addOrMergeItem finds the existing productId and calls increaseQuantity on that line, keeping its captured name and unit price. Verified in a probe (1 line, qty 4, unit 10.00).

items.prompt: In menu 3 the user enters 0.004 as a product price. What does the app print?
items.answer: Please enter a non-negative amount with at most 2 decimal places, for example 19.99.
distractors: Could not create product: Money must be greater than zero.
Created product with ID ... (stored at 0.00 after rounding the price)
Created product with ID ... (stored at 0.01 after rounding the price up)
items.explanation: readMoney passes the parsed value to DomainValues.money, whose setScale(2, UNNECESSARY) throws; readMoney catches it, prints its own hint and returns null, so the flow stops. Verified with piped input.

items.prompt: Why does FileDataStore rebuild orders with Order.restore instead of creating a DRAFT and replaying addOrMergeItem and setStatus?
items.answer: Replay hits the PAID edit block and moves updatedAt; restore avoids both
distractors: Replaying would be correct but slow, as each call recalculates every total
addOrMergeItem cannot add lines whose product is not in the catalog yet
restore skips validation entirely, so damaged files can still be repaired
items.explanation: A paid order loaded from disk must regain its items and discount without being reopened for editing or getting a new update time. restore builds the complete aggregate and validates it directly.

items.prompt: Startup finds a snapshot whose footer counts are wrong. What does the app do, and with which process exit status?
items.answer: It prints the Startup stopped message and reason, then exits with status 0
distractors: It prints the reason, then calls System.exit(1) so scripts see a failure
Starts with empty data and overwrites the snapshot on the next save
Falls back to the four legacy files, if they still exist, and continues
items.explanation: main catches the RuntimeException from load, prints "Startup stopped: ..." and "Existing data was not replaced..." and returns, so the JVM exits 0. Verified on data/sample-corrupt.

items.prompt: There is no oms.snapshot.txt, and the directory holds customers.txt, products.txt and orders.txt but no order_items.txt. What does load do?
items.answer: Fails with "Incomplete legacy dataset: all four files are required."
distractors: Loads the orders with no items, then writes a fresh snapshot on the next save
Ignores the three files and starts with an empty dataset
Loads the three files and creates order_items.txt on the next save
items.explanation: The loader counts how many of the four legacy files exist and refuses any count other than 0 or 4. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: The user chooses 13 (Exit), but the save fails because the data directory is read-only. What happens next?
items.answer: It reports the failure and keeps the session open for a retry
distractors: It reports the failure and exits, dropping the unsaved changes
It exits normally and retries the save automatically at next start
It writes the data to a backup file beside the snapshot and exits
items.explanation: exitApplication returns true (keep running) when saveData fails and prints "Data could not be saved. Session stays open so you can retry." Confirmed by reading the code; the course notes this branch was source-reviewed.

items.front: How are subtotal and total computed in the delivered Order, and why?
items.back: getSubtotal sums the current line totals and getTotal subtracts the discount. Deriving them leaves fewer facts to keep in sync; each OrderItem still keeps its own line total, maintained by its quantity method.

items.front: Give the order status transition graph.
items.back: DRAFT to SUBMITTED or CANCELLED; SUBMITTED to PAID or CANCELLED; PAID to SHIPPED or CANCELLED. SHIPPED and CANCELLED are terminal. Cancelling from PAID is a local status change only; there is no refund integration.

items.front: The aggregate, the snapshot validation and the atomic file save each protect something. What do none of them provide?
items.back: Authenticated ownership, concurrent request handling, cross-process stale-write detection, and payment idempotency. Those are the next lessons when the CLI becomes a web application.

items.front: What does the count footer in oms.snapshot.txt detect, and what does it not?
items.back: A mismatch detects ordinary truncation or missing records. It is not a checksum and does not resist intentional edits that also change the counts.
